lead: Tesla / TSLA — the drawdown is the entry point
smaller: Quantum computing / IONQ — the next AI trade
Gold / GLD — the only safe haven left
Prediction markets / HOOD — the Fed is now a bet
why_lead: Tesla is the trade where price and attention line up: TSLA closed at 236.26 on 2025-03-20, down 33.34% over 20 sessions, while the headlines carry holders being told to stick with the stock and short sellers booking a $16.2bn payday as BYD hit a record high. The crowd's simple story, that a drawdown in a believer's stock is a discount on the future, is repeated across Business Insider, Barron's and Fortune in the same week, and the index backdrop (S&P 500 down 7.43% over 20 sessions, VIX up 26.44%) gives it a cross-asset context.
why_smaller: Quantum is the retail trade where the stocks moved on a remark that same week, with Nvidia's chief executive saying he was wrong about the quantum timeline and surprised his comments hurt stocks, and IonQ down 9.27% and D-Wave down 18.02% in the 2025-03-20 session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-20).
Gold supplies the non-equity leg, with gold up 2.97% over 20 sessions and GLD up 3.60%, and the record-high and Citi $3,200 headlines are the anchors the crowd repeats.

Robinhood's prediction-markets hub gives the non-AI equity leg, with HOOD up 21.21% over five sessions while event contracts are a new product the crowd can ride and the regulatory settlements are the break.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir: down 17.77% over 20 sessions with strong Reddit and analyst headlines, but the attention is praise rather than a surge or a new catalyst that week.
Bitcoin and ether: flat or falling (bitcoin down 0.24% over 20 sessions, ether down 11.43%), so no surge to pair with the attention; both are covered in the crypto block.
XRP as a fourth trade: the SEC-case surge is real (up 13.47% over 20 sessions) but it overlaps the crypto block and a 4.37% reversal in the prior session weakens the price-attention pairing.
CoreWeave IPO: attention is high, but no eligible close exists in the card, so the price side of the test cannot be met.

Leveraged ETFs (TQQQ down 31.02%, SOXL down 37.13% over 20 sessions): a real drawdown with WSJ's free-fall headline, but it is the same risk-on tape as the Tesla lead rather than a separate narrative.
Nvidia GTC: the reaction headlines conflict (rose on analyst comfort, fell on the new chips), so no direction can be given.
Oklo and nuclear: a strong five-session move and a retail-facing agreement headline, kept in the catalyst block rather than the retail set.
